The science behind the scene.

Fractional distillation separates miscible liquids, especially when their boiling points are close. A fractionating column provides repeated condensation and vaporisation. The vapour becomes richer in the more volatile component as it rises.

Remember

  • Both components can vaporise together.
  • The column improves separation; it is not a filter.
  • The thermometer bulb sits near the side-arm, in the vapour path.
  • Cooling water enters the condenser at the lower end and leaves at the upper end.
  • A fraction is a portion collected during distillation, not necessarily a pure substance.

Model boundaries

Liquid A and Liquid B are fictional components. Particle colours, flows, enrichment and timing illustrate the idea; they do not predict temperatures, composition or purity. Some mixtures form azeotropes and cannot be completely separated by ordinary fractional distillation. The refinery view is a simplified industrial schematic.
